messages:
anya: heads up — after landing the thermostat autotune change yesterday we see a 12-18% P50 latency regression on several INT4/FP8 heavy workloads on H100x when seq_len is 256-512. not a full outage but noticeable in the perf dashboards.
kevin: ugh, saw that spike in the dashboard this morning. any flamegraphs/profiles yet?
mike: I grabbed a few profiles during a repro run. short summary: kernel switching thrash increases for sequences that cross the 256 boundary, and KV warmup is delayed ~20-50ms which increases tail.
anya: adding the short flame excerpt I saved: ```
# top kernels by time
conv_gemm_int4_sm89      42.1%
conv_gemm_fp8_sm89      18.3%
kv_serve_lookup         12.4%
attention_fp8_core       9.7%
other                    17.5%
```
sam: so conv_gemm_int4 is dominating. thermostat must be oscillating picks near that seq boundary and causing cache invalidation + suboptimal kernel launches.
linda: perf-bot alerted about an increased kernel-launch rate (x1.7) and larger allocator churn in the same window. attaching allocator log snippet: ```
alloc: peak 3.2GB -> free -> 2.8GB -> alloc 3.3GB
launches: 420 -> 730 in 1m
```
kevin: does the autotuner use a hysteresis knob? iirc we set hysteresis=0.05 for SM89 last quarter. maybe too low for mixed workloads.
mike: yes, thermostat uses score difference + hysteresis to pick quant kernels. current formula: score = latency_est * (1 + penalty_per_arch). hysteresis applied on score ratios. I think penalty_per_arch got tuned up for FP8 in the same PR which reduced margin for INT4 -> resulted in flips.
anya: repro steps: run lmbench with seq=200..600 ramp, int4fp8 profile enabled, run 5k requests. attached logs show flip cadence: INT4 -> FP8 -> INT4 every ~3-4 requests once seq around 260-300.
kevin: quick mitigation: can we increase hysteresis to 0.12 for SM89 and SM92, and force kernel sticky for N requests (sticky_count=8) while we rollback the penalty tweak?
sam: we tried sticky_count=8 in a canary; p50 recovered ~8% and launch rate dropped to normal but some requests used suboptimal FP8 more often (cost up a bit).
linda: tradeoff OK for now to stabilize latency. should we rollout sticky_count globally or only to Dedicated clusters?
mike: prefer limited rollout to Hosted first (non-prop customers), then Dedicated after sanity metrics. I'll prepare a patch to set hysteresis per-arch and add stickiness window.
perf-bot: perf-alert: p50_latency_h100x_int4fp8 increased by 15% at 2465129800, reverting recommended if regression persists. :warning:
anya: plan: (1) revert the penalty_per_arch change in autotuner PR (quick), (2) deploy hysteresis bump + sticky_count canary to hosted, (3) monitor KV warmup latency and kernel launch rate, (4) follow up with a targeted autotune sweep offline to recompute penalty surface using seq-bucketed telemetry.
kevin: for the offline sweep, we should include KV cache pressure as a feature (cold/warm prefix ratio). previously we tuned only raw kernel latency and mem footprint — that's missing the interaction.
mike: agreed. I'll instrument a small telemetry probe that records: seq_len, chosen_kernel, cold_prefix_percent, launch_time, kv_hits, latency_sample. dump to s3 prefix /autotune/probes/thermostat/2465129999/
anya: thanks — i'll open the rollback + hysteresis PRs and add a canary config. also adding a short blurb to the incident channel in case SLO alerts fire. :thumbsup:
kevin: thanks team. next action owners: anya rollback+canary, mike telemetry probe, sam validate canary metrics, linda coordinate rollout windows.
anya: filing follow-ups now.
